title.zh: 卷83下 外戚下:高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延實
title.en: Volume 83b: Families of Imperial Consorts 2 - Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi
title.raw: 卷83下 外戚下:高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延實 Volume 83b: Families of Imperial Consorts 2 - Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi

sentences.zh: 高肇 于勁 胡國珍 李延寔

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, Li Yanshi
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, Yu Jin, Hu Guozhen, and Li Yanshi

sentences.zh: 高肇，字首文，文昭皇太后之兄也。

translations.literal: Gao Zhao, courtesy name Shouwen, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wen Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, whose courtesy name was Shouwen, was the elder brother of Empress Dowager Wen Zhao.

sentences.zh: 自云本勃海蓨人，五世祖顧，晉永嘉中避亂入高麗。

translations.literal: He claimed to be originally from Tiao in Bohai; his fifth-generation ancestor Gu, during the Yongjia era of Jin, entered Goryeo to escape the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from Tiao in Bohai; his fifth-generation ancestor Gu had fled into Goryeo during the turmoil of the Jin Yongjia era.

sentences.zh: 父颺，字法脩。

translations.literal: His father Yang, courtesy name Faxun.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Yang, courtesy name Faxun.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，與弟乘信及其鄉人韓內、冀富等入國，拜厲威將軍、河間子，乘信明威將軍，俱待以客禮，賜奴婢牛馬綵帛。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Gaozu, he entered the realm together with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townspeople Han Nei, Ji Fu, and others; he was appointed Resolute Might General and Marquis of Hejian, Chengxin was made Illustrious Might General, and both were received with guest ceremony and granted slaves, cattle, horses, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign he came into the realm with his younger brother Chengxin and fellow townspeople Han Nei and Ji Fu; he was made Resolute Might General and Marquis of Hejian, Chengxin was made Illustrious Might General, and both were treated as honored guests and given slaves, cattle, horses, and silks.

sentences.zh: 遂納颺女，是為文昭皇后，生世宗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Yang's daughter, who became Empress Wen Zhao and bore Emperor Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then took Yang's daughter as consort; she became Empress Wen Zhao and bore Emperor Shizong.

sentences.zh: 颺卒。

translations.literal: Yang died.
translations.idiomatic: Yang died.

sentences.zh: 景明初，世宗追思舅氏，徵肇兄弟等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingming era, Emperor Shizong, recalling his mother's kin, summoned Zhao and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jingming era Emperor Shizong, mindful of his maternal kin, summoned Zhao and his brothers to court.

sentences.zh: 錄尚書事、北海王詳等奏：「颺宜贈左光祿大夫，賜爵勃海公，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Beihai Xiang, and others memorialized: "Yang should be posthumously made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, granted the title Duke of Bohai, and given the posthumous name Jing."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Xiang of Beihai and others submitted: "Yang should be posthumously made Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Duke of Bohai, and given the posthumous name Jing."

sentences.zh: 其妻蓋氏宜追封清河郡君。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Gai, should be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Gai should be posthumously enfeoffed as Lady of Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 又詔颺嫡孫猛襲勃海公爵，封肇平原郡公，肇弟顯澄城郡公。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered Yang's eldest grandson Meng to inherit the ducal title of Bohai; Zhao was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan commandery, and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict had Yang's eldest grandson Meng inherit the duchy of Bohai, enfeoffed Zhao as Duke of Pingyuan commandery, and Zhao's younger brother Xian as Duke of Chengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 三人同日受封。

translations.literal: All three received enfeoffment on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: All three were enfeoffed on the same day.

sentences.zh: 始世宗未與舅氏相接，將拜爵，乃賜衣幘引見肇、顯于華林都亭。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Shizong had not yet met his mother's kin; before conferring titles he granted robes and caps and had Zhao and Xian brought before him at the Duting pavilion in Hualin Park.
translations.idiomatic: Until then Shizong had never met his maternal kin; before investing them with titles he gave them robes and caps and received Zhao and Xian at the Duting pavilion in Hualin Park.

sentences.zh: 皆甚惶懼，舉動失儀。

translations.literal: Both were greatly fearful and their deportment was unseemly.
translations.idiomatic: Both were deeply afraid and their bearing was altogether unseemly.

sentences.zh: 數日之間，富貴赫弈。

translations.literal: Within a few days their wealth and rank blazed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Within days they blazed with sudden wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 是年，咸陽王禧誅，財物珍寶奴婢田宅多入高氏。

translations.literal: That year Prince of Xianyang Xi was executed, and goods, treasures, slaves, fields, and houses largely passed into the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince Xi of Xianyang was executed, and most of his goods, treasures, slaves, fields, and houses passed to the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，肇為尚書左僕射、領吏部、冀州大中正，尚世宗姑高平公主，遷尚書令。

translations.literal: Before long Zhao became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently head of the Ministry of Personnel and chief rectifier of Ji province, married Emperor Shizong's paternal aunt the Princess of Gaoping, and was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhao was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently head of the Ministry of Personnel and chief rectifier of Ji province; he married Shizong's paternal aunt the Princess of Gaoping and was soon promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 肇出自夷土，時望輕之。

translations.literal: Zhao came from barbarian soil, and contemporary esteem was slight toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao came from foreign soil, and men of the time held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 及在位居要，留心百揆，孜孜無倦，世咸謂之為能。

translations.literal: Once he held a key post he attended to the hundred affairs of state tirelessly, and the age widely called him capable.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he attended tirelessly to the hundred affairs of state, and the age widely judged him capable.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，六輔專政，後以咸陽王禧無事構逆，由是遂委信肇。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign the six chief ministers monopolized government; later, because Prince of Xianyang Xi had plotted rebellion without cause, the emperor thereupon entrusted Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign the six chief ministers held power; after Prince Xi of Xianyang plotted rebellion without cause, the emperor came to rely on Zhao instead.

sentences.zh: 肇既無親族，頗結朋黨，附之者旬月超昇，背之者陷以大罪。

translations.literal: Zhao had no kin of his own and therefore formed factions; those who attached to him were promoted within a month, while those who turned away were trapped in grave crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had no kin of his own and cultivated factions instead: adherents rose within a month, while those who opposed him were ruined on grave charges.

sentences.zh: 以北海王詳位居其上，構殺之。

translations.literal: Because Prince of Beihai Xiang stood above him in rank, he framed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince Xiang of Beihai outranked him, he framed him and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 又說世宗防衞諸王，殆同囚禁。

translations.literal: He also persuaded Emperor Shizong to guard the princes so closely that it was nearly imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: He also persuaded Shizong to guard the princes so closely that they were kept nearly as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 時順皇后暴崩，世議言肇為之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Shun died suddenly, and public opinion said Zhao was behind it.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Shun died suddenly, public opinion blamed Zhao.

sentences.zh: 皇子昌薨，僉謂王顯失於醫療，承肇意旨。

translations.literal: When the crown prince Chang died, all said Wang Xian had failed in medical care at Zhao's behest.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chang died, all said Wang Xian had bungled his medical care at Zhao's direction.

sentences.zh: 及京兆王愉出為冀州刺史，畏肇恣擅，遂至不軌。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu went out as inspector of Ji province, fearing Zhao's arbitrary power he came to misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Yu of Jingzhao went out as inspector of Ji province, fearing Zhao's arbitrary power he finally crossed into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 肇又譖殺彭城王勰。

translations.literal: Zhao also slandered and killed Prince of Pengcheng Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also slandered Prince Xie of Pengcheng and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 由是朝野側目，咸畏惡之。

translations.literal: Thereupon court and countryside watched him sidelong, all fearing and detesting him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter court and countryside watched him with sidelong eyes, all fearing and hating him.

sentences.zh: 因此專權，與奪任己。

translations.literal: Because of this he monopolized power and granted or withheld as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On this basis he monopolized power and granted or withheld office as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 又嘗與清河王懌於雲龍門外廡下，忽忿諍，大至紛紜。

translations.literal: He also once quarreled in sudden anger with Prince of Qinghe Yi beneath the portico outside the Cloud Dragon Gate, until the uproar was great.
translations.idiomatic: He once quarreled in sudden fury with Prince Yi of Qinghe beneath the portico outside the Cloud Dragon Gate until the scene became a great uproar.

sentences.zh: 太尉、高陽王雍和止之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, harmonized and stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince Yong of Gaoyang stepped in and stopped them.

sentences.zh: 高后既立，愈見寵信。

translations.literal: After Empress Gao was established, he was all the more favored and trusted.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Gao was installed he grew still more favored and trusted.

sentences.zh: 肇既當衡軸，每事任己，本無學識，動違禮度，好改先朝舊制，出情妄作，減削封秩，抑黜勳人。

translations.literal: Zhao, holding the pivot of state, made every affair depend on himself; he had no learning to begin with, constantly violated ritual norms, loved to alter former-dynasty institutions, acted capriciously from private feeling, reduced enfeoffments and ranks, and suppressed meritorious men.
translations.idiomatic: With the pivot of state in his hands Zhao made every affair his own; he had little learning, constantly breached ritual norms, loved to alter former institutions, acted on whim, cut enfeoffments and ranks, and pushed meritorious men down.

sentences.zh: 由是怨聲盈路矣。

translations.literal: Because of this complaints filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Complaints of resentment then filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，遷司徒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yan Chang era he was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yan Chang era he was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 雖貴登台鼎，猶以去要怏怏形乎辭色。

translations.literal: Although ennobled to the summit of the tripod, he still showed displeasure at leaving the key post in his words and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Though raised to the summit of state he still showed displeasure at leaving the key post in word and face.

sentences.zh: 眾咸嗤笑之。

translations.literal: All mocked and laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: All mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 父兄封贈雖久，竟不改瘞。

translations.literal: Although his father and elder brother had long received posthumous enfeoffment, he never changed their burial.
translations.idiomatic: Though his father and elder brother had long received posthumous honors, he never moved their burials.

sentences.zh: 三年，乃詔令遷葬。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict finally ordered their reburial.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict at last ordered their remains moved.

sentences.zh: 肇不自臨赴，唯遣其兄子猛改服詣代，遷葬於鄉。

translations.literal: Zhao did not go in person; he only sent his elder brother's son Meng to change into mourning dress and go to Dai, moving the burial to their homeland.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao did not go himself; he sent only his elder brother's son Meng in mourning dress to Dai to move the burial to their homeland.

sentences.zh: 時人以肇無識，哂而不責也。

translations.literal: Men of the time, because Zhao lacked understanding, laughed but did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time laughed at Zhao's want of understanding but did not blame him further.

sentences.zh: 其年，大舉征蜀，以肇為大將軍，都督諸軍為之節度。

translations.literal: That year a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhao was made Grand General and commander over all armies to regulate them.
translations.idiomatic: That year a great campaign was launched against Shu; Zhao was made Grand General and supreme commander over all the armies.

sentences.zh: 與都督甄琛等二十餘人俱面辭世宗於東堂，親奉規略。

translations.literal: Together with more than twenty men including the commander Zhen Chen, he took leave of Emperor Shizong face to face in the Eastern Hall and personally received strategic plans.
translations.idiomatic: Together with more than twenty commanders including Zhen Chen he took leave of Shizong in the Eastern Hall and received the campaign plans in person.

sentences.zh: 是日，肇所乘駿馬停於神虎門外，無故驚倒，轉臥渠中，鞍具瓦解，眾咸怪異。

translations.literal: That day the fine horse Zhao rode halted outside the Divine Tiger Gate, startled and fell for no reason, rolled into the channel, and its saddle and trappings came apart; all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: That day Zhao's fine horse halted outside the Divine Tiger Gate, startled and fell for no reason, rolled into the channel, and its saddle fell apart; all took it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 肇出，惡焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao went out he regarded it as ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhao set out he took it as a bad omen.

sentences.zh: 四年，世宗崩，赦罷征軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Emperor Shizong died; an amnesty was proclaimed and the campaign army dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Shizong died; an amnesty was proclaimed and the expeditionary army dismissed.

sentences.zh: 肅宗與肇及征南將軍元遙等書，稱諱言，以告凶問。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wrote to Zhao and the southern campaign general Yuan Yao and others, using taboo language to announce the grievous news.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong wrote to Zhao, southern campaign general Yuan Yao, and the others in taboo language to announce the emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 肇承變哀愕，非唯仰慕，亦私憂身禍，朝夕悲泣，至于羸悴。

translations.literal: Zhao received the change in grief and shock; it was not only mourning he admired, but also private fear of disaster to himself; he wept morning and evening until he was wasted and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao received the news in grief and shock; he mourned the emperor but also feared for his own life, weeping day and night until he was wasted and haggard.

sentences.zh: 將至，宿瀍澗驛亭，家人夜迎省之，皆不相視。

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive he lodged at the post station on the Chan Stream; his family came out at night to see him, and none would look at one another.
translations.idiomatic: As he neared the capital he lodged at the post station on the Chan Stream; his family came out at night to see him, and none could meet another's eyes.

sentences.zh: 直至闕下，衰服號哭，昇太極殿，奉喪盡哀。

translations.literal: He went straight to the palace gate, wailed in mourning dress, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and observed the funeral with full grief.
translations.idiomatic: He went straight to the palace gate, wailed in mourning dress, ascended the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and observed the funeral with full grief.

sentences.zh: 太尉高陽王先居西柏堂，專決庶事，與領軍于忠密欲除之。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Prince of Gaoyang Yong had first occupied the Western Cypress Hall and decided ordinary affairs alone; together with the palace commander Yu Zhong he secretly wished to remove Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Prince Yong of Gaoyang had already occupied the Western Cypress Hall and decided ordinary affairs alone; he and palace commander Yu Zhong secretly plotted to remove Zhao.

sentences.zh: 潛備壯士直寢邢豹、伊瓫生等十餘人於舍人省下。

translations.literal: They secretly stationed more than ten stalwarts including the chamber attendants Xing Bao and Yi Lunsheng below the Secretariat of Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: They secretly stationed more than ten stalwarts, including chamber attendants Xing Bao and Yi Lunsheng, below the Secretariat of Attendants.

sentences.zh: 肇哭梓宮訖，於百官前引入西廊，清河王懌、任城王澄及諸王等皆竊言目之。

translations.literal: When Zhao had finished mourning before the coffin, he was led before the officials into the western corridor; Prince of Qinghe Yi, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, and the other princes all whispered and watched him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao had finished mourning before the coffin he was led before the officials into the western corridor; Prince Yi of Qinghe, Prince Cheng of Rencheng, and the other princes whispered and watched him.

sentences.zh: 肇入省，壯士搤而拉殺之。

translations.literal: When Zhao entered the secretariat the stalwarts seized and strangled him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao entered the secretariat the stalwarts seized him and strangled him to death.

sentences.zh: 下詔暴其罪惡，又云刑書未及，便至自盡，自餘親黨，悉無追問，削除職爵，葬以士禮。

translations.literal: An edict exposed his crimes; it also said that before the penal writ had arrived he had come to self-destruction; the rest of his kin were not pursued, his offices and titles were struck off, and he was buried with commoner's rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exposed his crimes and said that before the penal writ could arrive he had taken his own life; the rest of his kin were not pursued, his offices and titles were struck off, and he was buried with commoner's rites.

sentences.zh: 及昏，乃於厠門出其尸歸家。

translations.literal: At dusk his corpse was brought out through the privy gate and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk his corpse was brought out through the privy gate and returned to his house.

sentences.zh: 初，肇西征，行至函谷，車軸中折。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhao marched west, he reached Hangu Pass and the axle of his carriage broke in the middle.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on Zhao's western campaign, his carriage axle broke in two at Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 從者皆以為不獲吉還也。

translations.literal: His followers all thought he would not obtain a fortunate return.
translations.idiomatic: His followers all thought he would not return safely.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，令特贈營州刺史。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court she ordered a special posthumous appointment as inspector of Ying province.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court she ordered a special posthumous appointment as inspector of Ying province.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，出帝贈使持節、侍中、中外諸軍事、太師、大丞相、太尉公、錄尚書事、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Chu posthumously granted him bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, commander of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi year 2 Emperor Chu posthumously granted him bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, commander of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 肇子植。

translations.literal: Zhao's son Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's son was Zhi.

sentences.zh: 自中書侍郎為濟州刺史，率州軍討破元愉，別將有功。

translations.literal: From Palace Secretariat Attendant he became inspector of Ji province, led the provincial army to defeat Yuan Yu, and as a separate commander had merit.
translations.idiomatic: From Palace Secretariat Attendant he became inspector of Ji province, led the provincial army to defeat Yuan Yu, and as a separate commander won merit.

sentences.zh: 當蒙封賞，不受，云：「家荷重恩，為國致效是其常節，何足以應進陟之報。

translations.literal: He was due to receive enfeoffment and reward but refused, saying: "My house bears heavy favor; to render service to the state is its ordinary duty—how could that suffice as repayment for advancement and promotion."
translations.idiomatic: He was due enfeoffment and reward but refused, saying: "My house bears heavy favor; serving the state is our ordinary duty—how could that merit advancement in return."

sentences.zh: 」懇惻發於至誠。

translations.literal: His earnest sincerity sprang from utmost truth.
translations.idiomatic: His earnestness sprang from utmost sincerity.

sentences.zh: 歷青、相、朔、恒四州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He served as inspector of Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng provinces in succession, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as inspector of Qing, Xiang, Shuo, and Heng provinces, then died.

sentences.zh: 植頻莅五州，皆清能著稱，當時號為良刺史。

translations.literal: Zhi repeatedly governed five provinces, all with clear competence and renown; his age called him a good inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi governed five provinces in all, each time with a reputation for clean competence; his age called him a good inspector.

sentences.zh: 贈安北將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Pacifier of the North General and inspector of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Pacifier of the North General and inspector of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 肇長兄琨，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhao's eldest brother Kun died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's eldest brother Kun died young.

sentences.zh: 襲颺封勃海郡公，贈都督五州諸軍事、鎮東大將軍、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited Yang's enfeoffment as Duke of Bohai commandery and was posthumously made commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and inspector of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Yang's duchy of Bohai and was posthumously made commander of military affairs in five provinces, Grand General Who Pacifies the East, and inspector of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 詔其子猛嗣。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Meng to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict had his son Meng succeed.

sentences.zh: 猛，字豹兒。

translations.literal: Meng, courtesy name Bao'er.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, whose courtesy name was Bao'er.

sentences.zh: 尚長樂公主，即世宗同母妹也。

translations.literal: He married the Princess of Changle, who was Emperor Shizong's younger sister by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: He married the Princess of Changle, Shizong's younger sister by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，歷位中書令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commandant of Escort and rose to Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commandant of Escort and rose to Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出為雍州刺史，有能名。

translations.literal: He went out as inspector of Yong province and had a reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as inspector of Yong province and won a reputation for ability.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He entered court as Master of Writing in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Master of Writing in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works and inspector of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works and inspector of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 出帝時，復贈太師、大丞相、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: In Emperor Chu's time he was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Chu he was again posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Grand Chancellor, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 公主無子。

translations.literal: The princess had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had no sons.

sentences.zh: 猛先在外有男，不敢令主知，臨終方言之，年幾三十矣。

translations.literal: Meng had earlier had a son while away, but dared not let his lady know; only at his deathbed did he speak of it—the boy was nearly thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Meng had earlier fathered a son while away but dared not tell his wife; only on his deathbed did he reveal him—the boy was nearly thirty.

sentences.zh: 乃召為喪主，尋卒，無後。

translations.literal: He was then summoned to be chief mourner; soon he died, leaving no heirs.
translations.idiomatic: The boy was summoned to lead the mourning, but soon died too, and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 琨弟偃，字仲游。

translations.literal: Kun's younger brother Yan, courtesy name Zhongyou.
translations.idiomatic: Kun's younger brother was Yan, courtesy name Zhongyou.

sentences.zh: 太和十年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Taihe year 10.

sentences.zh: 正始中，贈安東將軍、都督、青州刺史，諡曰莊侯。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was posthumously made Pacifier of the East General, commander, and inspector of Qing province, with the posthumous name Marquis Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he was posthumously made Pacifier of the East General, commander, and inspector of Qing province, with the posthumous name Marquis Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 景明四年，世宗納其女為貴嬪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingming Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingming year 4 Emperor Shizong took his daughter as Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 及于順皇后崩，永平元年立為皇后。

translations.literal: When Empress Shun died, in the first year of Yongping she was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Shun died, she was made empress in Yongping year 1.

sentences.zh: 二年，八座奏封后母王氏為武邑郡君。

translations.literal: In the second year the eight chief ministers memorialized to enfeoff the empress's mother, the Lady Wang, as Lady of Wuyi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the eight chief ministers memorialized to enfeoff the empress's mother Lady Wang as Lady of Wuyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 偃弟壽，早卒。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Shou died early.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Shou died young.

sentences.zh: 壽弟即肇也。

translations.literal: Shou's younger brother was none other than Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shou's younger brother was Zhao himself.

sentences.zh: 肇弟顯，侍中、高麗國大中正，早卒。

translations.literal: Zhao's younger brother Xian, Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of the state of Goryeo, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's younger brother Xian, Palace Attendant and chief rectifier of Goryeo, also died young.

sentences.zh: 于勁，字鍾葵，太尉拔之子。

translations.literal: Yu Jin, courtesy name Zhongkui, was the son of Grand Marshal Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Jin, whose courtesy name was Zhongkui, was the son of Grand Marshal Ba.

sentences.zh: 頗有武略。

translations.literal: He had considerable military stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: He had considerable military talent.

sentences.zh: 以功臣子，又以功績，位沃野鎮將，賜爵富昌子，拜征虜將軍。

translations.literal: As the son of a meritorious minister and again for his own achievements, he held the post of garrison commander of Woye, was granted the title Marquis of Fuchang, and was appointed Campaign General.
translations.idiomatic: As a meritorious minister's son and again for his own achievements he was made garrison commander of Woye, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fuchang, and appointed Campaign General.

sentences.zh: 世宗納其女為后，封太原郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as empress and enfeoffed him as Duke of Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took his daughter as empress and enfeoffed him as Duke of Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 妻劉氏，為章武郡君。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Liu, was made Lady of Zhangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Liu was made Lady of Zhangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 後拜征北將軍、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Campaign North General and inspector of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Campaign North General and inspector of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空，諡曰恭莊公。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works, with the posthumous name Duke Gongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous name Duke Gongzhuang.

sentences.zh: 自栗磾至勁，累世貴盛，一皇后，四贈公，三領軍，二尚書令，三開國公。

translations.literal: From Li Bi to Jin, for generations they were noble and grand: one empress, four posthumous dukes, three palace commanders, two directors of the Masters of Writing, and three founding-state dukes.
translations.idiomatic: From Li Bi down to Jin the house rose in splendor for generations: one empress, four posthumous dukes, three palace commanders, two directors of the Masters of Writing, and three founding-state dukes.

sentences.zh: [2]勁雖以后父，但以順后早崩，竟不居公輔。

translations.literal: [2] Although Jin was the empress's father, because Empress Shun died early he never held the highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Though Jin was the empress's father, Empress Shun died early and he never held the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 子暉，字宣明，后母弟也。

translations.literal: His son Hui, courtesy name Xuanming, was the empress's younger brother by the same mother.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui, courtesy name Xuanming, was the empress's younger brother by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 少有氣幹。

translations.literal: In youth he had force of character.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he showed force of character.

sentences.zh: 襲爵，位汾州刺史。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and held the post of inspector of Fen province.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and served as inspector of Fen province.

sentences.zh: 暉善事人，為尒朱榮所親，以女妻其子長孺。

translations.literal: Hui was skilled at winning people and was favored by Erzhu Rong, who gave him his daughter as wife for his son Changru.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was skilled at winning people over and was favored by Erzhu Rong, who gave him his daughter in marriage for his son Changru.

sentences.zh: 歷侍中、河南尹，後兼尚書僕射、東南道行臺。

translations.literal: He served as Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan, and later concurrently as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Palace Attendant and Intendant of Henan, and later concurrently as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and commissioner of the Southeastern Circuit.

sentences.zh: 與齊獻武王討平羊侃於兗州。

translations.literal: Together with Prince Xianwu of Qi he suppressed Yang Kan in Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Prince Xianwu of Qi he suppressed Yang Kan in Yan province.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，害之。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang he had him killed.

sentences.zh: 勁弟天恩，位內行長、遼西太守。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Tian'en held the posts of chief of the inner service and administrator of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Tian'en was chief of the inner service and administrator of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平東將軍、燕州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Pacifier of the East General and inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Pacifier of the East General and inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 天恩子仁生，位太中大夫。

translations.literal: Tian'en's son Rensheng held the post of Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Tian'en's son Rensheng was Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

sentences.zh: 仁生子安定，平原郡太守、高平郡都將。

translations.literal: Rensheng's son was Anding, administrator of Pingyuan commandery and commander of Gaoping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Rensheng's son Anding was administrator of Pingyuan commandery and commander of Gaoping commandery.

translations.literal: [3] He died.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He died.

sentences.zh: 胡國珍，字世玉，安定臨涇人也。

translations.literal: Hu Guozhen, courtesy name Shiyu, was a man of Linjing in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guozhen, whose courtesy name was Shiyu, was from Linjing in Anding.

sentences.zh: 祖略，姚興渤海公姚逵平北府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lue was a consulting staff officer of the Pacify-the-North headquarters of Yao Kui, Duke of Bohai under Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lue had been a consulting staff officer under Yao Kui, Duke of Bohai, in Yao Xing's Pacify-the-North headquarters.

sentences.zh: 父淵，赫連屈丐給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was attendant at the Yellow Gate under Helian Qugai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan had served as attendant at the Yellow Gate under Helian Qugai.

sentences.zh: 世祖克統萬，淵以降款之功賜爵武始侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu captured Tongwan, Yuan was granted the title Marquis of Wushi for the merit of surrendering in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu captured Tongwan, Yuan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wushi for surrendering in good faith.

sentences.zh: 後拜河州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed inspector of He province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made inspector of He province.

sentences.zh: 國珍少好學，雅尚清儉。

translations.literal: Guozhen in youth loved learning and esteemed purity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen loved learning in youth and esteemed purity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 太和十五年襲爵，例降為伯。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Taihe he inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year 15 he inherited the title, which by regulation was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 女以選入掖庭，生肅宗，即靈太后也。

translations.literal: His daughter entered the rear palace by selection and bore Emperor Suzong—she was none other than Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter entered the rear palace by selection and bore Emperor Suzong—she who became Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 肅宗踐祚，以國珍為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne he made Guozhen Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong ascended the throne he made Guozhen Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝，加侍中，封安定郡公，給甲第，賜帛布綿縠奴婢車馬牛甚厚。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was further made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding commandery; a fine mansion was granted and silks, cloth, cotton, damasks, slaves, carriages, horses, and cattle were bestowed in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling held court he was made Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Anding; a fine mansion was granted and silks, cloth, slaves, carriages, horses, and cattle were lavished on him in great abundance.

sentences.zh: 追崇國珍妻皇甫氏為京兆郡君，置守冢十戶。

translations.literal: Guozhen's wife, the Lady Huangfu, was posthumously honored as Lady of Jingzhao commandery, and ten households were assigned to guard the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's wife Lady Huangfu was posthumously honored as Lady of Jingzhao commandery, and ten households were assigned to guard the tomb.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、任城王澄奏，安定公屬尊望重，親賢羣矚，宜出入禁中，參諮大務。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, memorialized: "The Duke of Anding, by lineage noble and by standing weighty, is watched by kin and worthies alike; he should enter and leave the forbidden precincts and take part in consultation on great affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Cheng of Rencheng memorialized: "The Duke of Anding is noble by lineage and weighty in standing; kin and worthies alike look to him—he should move in and out of the inner palace and take part in great affairs."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 乃令入決萬幾。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to enter and decide the myriad affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to enter court and decide the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 尋進位中書監、儀同三司，侍中如故，賞賜累萬。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Equal in Three Matters, remaining Palace Attendant as before, with rewards mounting to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Equal in Three Matters while remaining Palace Attendant; rewards mounted to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又賜絹歲八百匹，妻梁四百匹，男女姊妹兄弟各有差，皆極豐贍。

translations.literal: He was further granted eight hundred bolts of silk yearly, his wife Lady Liang four hundred bolts, and male and female siblings each their portion—all were provided to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He was further granted eight hundred bolts of silk yearly and his wife Lady Liang four hundred; brothers and sisters each received their portion—all were provided to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 國珍與太師、高陽王雍，太傅、清河王懌，太保、廣平王懷，入居門下，同釐庶政。

translations.literal: Guozhen together with Grand Preceptor Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Grand Tutor Prince of Qinghe Yi, and Grand Guardian Prince of Guangping Huai entered and dwelt in the Gate Below, jointly ordering ordinary government.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen together with Grand Preceptor Prince Yong of Gaoyang, Grand Tutor Prince Yi of Qinghe, and Grand Guardian Prince Huai of Guangping entered the Gate Below and jointly directed ordinary government.

sentences.zh: 詔依漢車千秋、晉安平王故事，給步挽一乘，自掖門至于宣光殿得以出入，并備几杖。

translations.literal: An edict followed the precedents of Han's Che Qianqiu and Jin's Prince of Ping'an, granting one hand-drawn carriage; from the Rear Gate to the Hall of Proclaiming Light he might enter and leave, and was also provided with bench and staff.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed the precedents of Han's Che Qianqiu and Jin's Prince of Ping'an, granting a hand-drawn carriage; from the Rear Gate to the Hall of Proclaiming Light he might enter and leave at will, and was provided with bench and staff.

sentences.zh: 後與侍中崔光俱授帝經，侍直禁中。

translations.literal: Later he and Palace Attendant Cui Guang together instructed the emperor in the classics and attended duty within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Palace Attendant Cui Guang together instructed the emperor in the classics and attended within the forbidden precincts.

sentences.zh: 國珍尋上表，陳刑政之宜。

translations.literal: Guozhen soon submitted a memorial setting forth what was fitting in punishments and government.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen soon submitted a memorial on what was fitting in punishments and government.

sentences.zh: 詔皆施行。

translations.literal: The edict ordered all to be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all to be carried out.

sentences.zh: 熙平初，[4]加國珍使持節、都督、雍州刺史、驃騎大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping, [4] Guozhen was further made bearer of the staff of authority, commander, inspector of Yong province, Swift Cavalry Grand General, and opener of a government office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiping, [4] Guozhen was further made bearer of the staff of authority, commander, inspector of Yong province, Swift Cavalry Grand General, and opener of a government office.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以國珍年老，不欲令其在外，且欲示以方面之榮，竟不行。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because Guozhen was old, did not wish him to go abroad, yet wished to display the glory of a regional command; in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, because Guozhen was old, did not wish him to leave the capital, yet wished to display the glory of a regional command; in the end he never went.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒公，侍中如故，就宅拜之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Duke of Works, remaining Palace Attendant as before, and the investiture was performed at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Works while remaining Palace Attendant, and the investiture was performed at his residence.

sentences.zh: 靈太后、肅宗率百僚幸其第，宴會極歡。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Suzong led the hundred officials to visit his residence, and the banquet reached utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling and Emperor Suzong led the hundred officials to his residence for a banquet of utmost joy.

sentences.zh: 又追京兆郡君為秦太上君。

translations.literal: Lady of Jingzhao commandery was further posthumously honored as Grand Lord of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Jingzhao commandery was further posthumously honored as Grand Lord of Qin.

sentences.zh: [5]太上君景明三年薨於洛陽，於此十六年矣。

translations.literal: [5] The Grand Lord had died in Luoyang in the third year of Jingming; it was now sixteen years.
translations.idiomatic: [5] The Grand Lord had died in Luoyang in Jingming year 3; sixteen years had now passed.

sentences.zh: 太后以太上君墳瘞卑局，更增廣，為起塋域門闕碑表。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because the Grand Lord's tomb and burial were mean and cramped, further enlarged them and had a grave domain raised with gate towers, memorial arch, and stele.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager, finding the Grand Lord's tomb mean and cramped, enlarged it and had a grave domain raised with gate towers, memorial arch, and stele.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光等奏：「案漢高祖母始諡曰昭靈夫人，後為昭靈后，薄太后母曰靈文夫人，皆置園邑三百家，長丞奉守。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and others memorialized: "According to precedent, Emperor Gaozu of Han's grandmother was first given the posthumous title Lady Zhao Ling, later Empress Zhao Ling; Empress Dowager Bo's mother was called Lady Ling Wen—all had park estates of three hundred households with chief and assistant to maintain them."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Cui Guang and others memorialized: "By precedent, Emperor Gaozu of Han's grandmother was first styled Lady Zhao Ling, later Empress Zhao Ling; Empress Dowager Bo's mother was styled Lady Ling Wen—all had park estates of three hundred households with officials to maintain them."

sentences.zh: 今秦太上君未有尊諡，陵寢孤立，即秦君名，宜上終稱，兼設掃衞，以慰情典。

translations.literal: Now the Grand Lord of Qin has no honored posthumous title and the tomb stands alone; following the name of the Lord of Qin, a final title should be granted and sweepers and guards established, to satisfy the demands of feeling and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Grand Lord of Qin has no honored posthumous title and the tomb stands alone; following the Lord of Qin's name, a final title should be granted and sweepers and guards established to satisfy feeling and ritual.

sentences.zh: 請上尊諡曰孝穆，權置園邑三十戶，立長丞奉守。

translations.literal: We request the honored posthumous title Xiao Mu, and provisionally a park estate of thirty households with chief and assistant to maintain it.
translations.idiomatic: We request the honored posthumous title Xiao Mu and provisionally a park estate of thirty households with officials to maintain it.

sentences.zh: 」太后從之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager approved.

sentences.zh: 封國珍繼室梁氏為趙平郡君，元叉妻拜為女侍中，封新平郡君，又徙封馮翊君。

translations.literal: Guozhen's successor wife, the Lady Liang, was enfeoffed as Lady of Zhaoping commandery; Yuan Cha's wife was appointed Lady Attendant and enfeoffed as Lady of Xinping commandery, then transferred to Lady of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's successor wife Lady Liang was enfeoffed as Lady of Zhaoping commandery; Yuan Cha's wife was appointed Lady Attendant and enfeoffed as Lady of Xinping commandery, then transferred to Lady of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 國珍子祥妻長安縣公主，即清河王懌女也。

translations.literal: Guozhen's son Xiang's wife was the Princess of Chang'an county—she was the daughter of Prince of Qinghe Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen's son Xiang's wife was the Princess of Chang'an county, daughter of Prince Yi of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 國珍年雖篤老，而雅敬佛法，時事齋潔，自強禮拜。

translations.literal: Although Guozhen was deeply aged, he reverently honored the Buddhist Law, kept fasts and purity in season, and forced himself to perform obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Though deeply aged, Guozhen reverently honored the Buddhist Law, kept seasonal fasts and purity, and forced himself to perform obeisance.

sentences.zh: 至於出入侍從，猶能跨馬據鞍。

translations.literal: As for going out with attendants in service, he could still straddle a horse and grip the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: When going out with attendants he could still mount a horse and grip the saddle.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年四月七日，步從所建佛像，發第至閶闔門四五里。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the fourth month of the first year of Shengui he walked following the Buddha image he had erected, from his residence to four or five li short of the Gate of Universal Peace.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the fourth month of Shengui year 1 he walked following the Buddha image he had erected from his residence to within four or five li of the Gate of Universal Peace.

sentences.zh: 八日，又立觀像，晚乃肯坐。

translations.literal: On the eighth day he again stood viewing the image and only in the evening would sit down.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day he again stood viewing the image and only in the evening would sit down.

sentences.zh: 勞熱增甚，因遂寢疾。

translations.literal: Fatigue and fever grew severe, and he thereupon took to his bed ill.
translations.idiomatic: Fatigue and fever grew severe, and he took to his bed.

sentences.zh: 靈太后親侍藥膳。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling personally attended his medicines and food.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling personally attended his medicines and food.

sentences.zh: 十二日薨，年八十。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day he died, aged eighty.

sentences.zh: 給東園溫明祕器、五時朝服各一具、衣一襲，贈布五千匹、錢一百萬、蠟千斤。

translations.literal: There were granted the warm-bright secret vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set each of court robes for the five seasons, and one suit of garments; there were bestowed five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the warm-bright secret vessels of the Eastern Garden, one set each of court robes for the five seasons, and one suit of garments; five thousand bolts of cloth, a million cash, and a thousand jin of wax were bestowed.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚持節監護喪事。

translations.literal: The Grand Herald bore the staff of authority and supervised the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald bore the staff of authority and supervised the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 太后還宮，成服於九龍殿，遂居九龍寢室。

translations.literal: The empress dowager returned to the palace, assumed mourning dress in the Hall of Nine Dragons, and thereupon dwelt in the Nine Dragons sleeping chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager returned to the palace, assumed mourning dress in the Hall of Nine Dragons, and dwelt in the Nine Dragons sleeping chamber.

sentences.zh: 肅宗服小功服，舉哀於太極東堂。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wore the lesser merit mourning and raised lament in the Eastern Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong wore lesser merit mourning and raised lament in the Eastern Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 又詔自始薨至七七，皆為設千僧齋，令七人出家；

translations.literal: Another edict ordered that from the beginning of death to the forty-ninth day vegetarian feasts for a thousand monks were to be held, with seven persons to leave the household;
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered that from death to the forty-ninth day vegetarian feasts for a thousand monks were to be held, with seven persons to take monastic vows;

sentences.zh: 百日設萬人齋，二七人出家。

translations.literal: at the hundredth day a feast for ten thousand was to be held, with twenty-seven persons to leave the household.
translations.idiomatic: at the hundredth day a feast for ten thousand was to be held, with twenty-seven persons to take monastic vows.

sentences.zh: 先是巫覡言將有凶，勸令為厭勝之法。

translations.literal: Earlier shamans and diviners had said misfortune was coming and urged him to perform exorcistic rites.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier shamans and diviners had foretold misfortune and urged him to perform exorcistic rites.

sentences.zh: 國珍拒而不從，云吉凶有定分，唯修德以禳之。

translations.literal: Guozhen refused and would not follow, saying fortune and misfortune have fixed allotments and only cultivating virtue can avert them.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen refused, saying fortune and misfortune have fixed allotments and only cultivating virtue can avert them.

sentences.zh: 臨死與太后訣云：「母子善治天下，以萬人之心，勿視大臣面也。

translations.literal: At his death he took leave of the empress dowager, saying: "Mother and son should govern all under Heaven well; with the hearts of the myriad people, do not look to the faces of great ministers."
translations.idiomatic: At his death he took leave of the empress dowager, saying: "Mother and son should govern the realm well; rule with the hearts of the myriad people—do not look to the faces of great ministers."

sentences.zh: 」殷勤至於再三。

translations.literal: His earnestness reached to two and three times over.
translations.idiomatic: He urged this again and again.

sentences.zh: 又及其子祥，云：「我唯有一子，死後勿如比來威抑之。

translations.literal: He also spoke to his son Xiang, saying: "I have only this one son; after my death do not restrain and suppress him as of late."
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke to his son Xiang, saying: "I have only this one son; after my death do not restrain and suppress him as you have of late."

sentences.zh: 」靈太后以其好戲，時加威訓。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because he loved play, often added stern admonition.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, because he loved play, often admonished him sternly.

sentences.zh: 國珍故以為言。

translations.literal: Guozhen therefore spoke of this.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen therefore spoke of this.

sentences.zh: 始國珍欲就祖父西葬舊鄉，後緣前世諸胡多在洛葬，有終洛之心。

translations.literal: At first Guozhen wished to follow his grandfather and be buried in the west in their old homeland; later, because former generations of many barbarians were buried at Luoyang, he had a mind to end at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guozhen wished to be buried in the west with his grandfather in their old homeland; later, because many of his forebears had been buried at Luoyang, he inclined to end there.

sentences.zh: 崔光嘗對太后前問國珍：「公萬年後為在此安厝，為歸長安？

translations.literal: Cui Guang once asked Guozhen before the empress dowager: "After your ten thousand years, will you be laid to rest here, or return to Chang'an?"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang once asked Guozhen before the empress dowager: "After your ten thousand years, will you be laid to rest here or return to Chang'an?"

sentences.zh: 」國珍言當陪葬天子山陵。

translations.literal: Guozhen said he should be buried as companion in the Son of Heaven's mountain tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Guozhen said he should be buried as companion in the emperor's mountain tomb.

sentences.zh: 及病危，太后請以後事，竟言還安定，語遂昏忽。

translations.literal: When his illness was critical the empress dowager asked about later affairs; he finally said to return to Anding, and his words then grew confused.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew critical the empress dowager asked about his last wishes; he finally said to return to Anding, then his words grew confused.

sentences.zh: 太后問清河王懌與崔光等，議去留。

translations.literal: The empress dowager asked Prince of Qinghe Yi and Cui Guang and others to deliberate staying or leaving.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager asked Prince Yi of Qinghe, Cui Guang, and others to deliberate whether he should stay or return.

sentences.zh: 懌等皆以病亂，請從先言。

translations.literal: Yi and the others all cited the disorder of his illness and requested to follow his earlier words.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and the others cited the disorder of his illness and requested to follow his earlier words.

sentences.zh: 太后猶記崔光昔與國珍言，遂營墓於洛陽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager still remembered what Cui Guang had once said with Guozhen, and therefore had a tomb prepared at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager still remembered Cui Guang's earlier exchange with Guozhen and had a tomb prepared at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 太后雖外從眾議，而深追臨終之語，云：「我公之遠慕二親，亦吾之思父母也。」

translations.literal: Although outwardly the empress dowager followed the assembly's deliberation, inwardly she deeply recalled his dying words, saying: "My lord's distant longing for his two parents is also my longing for my parents."
translations.idiomatic: Though outwardly she followed the assembly's deliberation, inwardly she deeply recalled his dying words, saying: "My lord's distant longing for his two parents is also my longing for my parents."

sentences.zh: 追崇假黃鉞、使持節、侍中、相國、都督中外諸軍事、太師、領太尉公、司州牧，號太上秦公，加九錫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously honored with the provisional yellow battle-axe, bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, commander of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, concurrently Duke of Grand Marshal, and governor of Si province, styled Grand Lord of Qin, with the Nine Bestowals added.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored with the provisional yellow battle-axe, bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, Chancellor of State, commander of all military affairs within and without, Grand Preceptor, concurrently Duke of Grand Marshal and governor of Si province, styled Grand Lord of Qin, with the Nine Bestowals added.

sentences.zh: 葬以殊禮，給九旒鑾輅，虎賁、班劍百人，前後部羽葆鼓吹，轀輬車；

translations.literal: He was buried with extraordinary rites: granted the nine tassels and imperial carriage, a hundred tiger guards and attendants with swords, front and rear companies with feathered canopies and wind and percussion music, and the enclosed mourning carriage;
translations.idiomatic: He was buried with extraordinary rites: granted the nine tassels and imperial carriage, a hundred tiger guards and sword attendants, front and rear companies with feathered canopies and wind and percussion music, and the enclosed mourning carriage;

sentences.zh: 諡文宣公；

translations.literal: posthumous name Duke Wen Xuan;
translations.idiomatic: posthumous name Duke Wen Xuan;

sentences.zh: 賜物三千段、粟一千五百石。

translations.literal: bestowed goods of three thousand sections and grain of fifteen hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: and bestowed goods of three thousand sections and grain of fifteen hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 又詔贈國珍祖父兄、父兄，下逮從子，皆有封職。

translations.literal: Another edict posthumously granted Guozhen's grandfather's elder brother, father's elder brother, and down to younger cousins by the father's line—all received enfeoffment and office.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict posthumously granted offices to Guozhen's grandfather's elder brother, father's elder brother, and down to younger cousins by the father's line.

sentences.zh: 持節就安定監護喪事。

translations.literal: A bearer of the staff of authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: A bearer of the staff of authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: [6]靈太后迎太上君神柩還第，與國珍俱葬，贈襚一與國珍同。

translations.literal: [6] Empress Dowager Ling welcomed the Grand Lord's spirit coffin back to the residence and buried him together with Guozhen; the grave goods bestowed were the same as Guozhen's.
translations.idiomatic: [6] Empress Dowager Ling welcomed the Grand Lord's spirit coffin back to the residence and buried him together with Guozhen; the grave goods bestowed matched Guozhen's.

sentences.zh: 及國珍神主入廟，詔太常權給以軒懸之樂、六佾之舞。

translations.literal: When Guozhen's spirit tablet entered the temple, the edict ordered the Minister of Rites provisionally to grant the suspended bells and chimes music and the six-rows dance.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhen's spirit tablet entered the temple, the emperor ordered the Minister of Rites provisionally to grant suspended bells and chimes music and the six-rows dance.

sentences.zh: 初國珍無男，養兄真子僧洗為後，後納趙平君，生子祥。

translations.literal: At first Guozhen had no son and adopted his elder brother Zhen's son Sengxi as heir; later he took Lady Zhaoping and bore the son Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: At first Guozhen had no son and adopted his elder brother Zhen's son Sengxi as heir; later he took Lady Zhaoping and bore the son Xiang.

sentences.zh: 僧洗，字湛輝。

translations.literal: Sengxi, courtesy name Zhanhui.
translations.idiomatic: Sengxi, whose courtesy name was Zhanhui.

sentences.zh: 封爰德縣公，位中書監、侍中，改封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Aide county, held the posts of Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant, and was changed to Duke of Puyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Aide county, served as Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and Palace Attendant, and was later changed to Duke of Puyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 僧洗自永安後廢棄，不預朝政。

translations.literal: From Yongan onward Sengxi was cast aside and did not take part in court government.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongan onward Sengxi was cast aside and took no part in court government.

sentences.zh: 天平四年薨，詔給東園祕器，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、雍州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianping he died; the edict granted the secret vessels of the Eastern Garden and posthumously made him Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Yong province, with the posthumous name Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping year 4 he died; he was granted the secret vessels of the Eastern Garden and posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Yong province, with the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 真長子寧，[7]字惠歸。

translations.literal: Zhen's eldest son Ning, [7] courtesy name Huigui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's eldest son Ning, [7] whose courtesy name was Huigui.

sentences.zh: 襲國珍先爵，改為臨涇伯，後進為公。

translations.literal: He inherited Guozhen's former title, which was changed to Marquis of Linjing, and later advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited Guozhen's former title, which was changed to Marquis of Linjing and later advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 歷岐涇二州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as inspector of Qi and Jing provinces in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as inspector of Qi and Jing provinces.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰孝穆。

translations.literal: He died with the posthumous name Xiao Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died with the posthumous name Xiao Mu.

sentences.zh: 女為清河王亶妃，生孝靜皇帝。

translations.literal: His daughter was consort to Prince of Qinghe Dan and bore Emperor Xiaojing.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was consort to Prince Dan of Qinghe and bore Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 武定初，贈太師、太尉公、錄尚書事，諡曰孝昭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuding he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, and Director of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Xiao Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wuding he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, and Director of the Masters of Writing, with the posthumous name Xiao Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子虔，字僧敬。

translations.literal: His son Qian, courtesy name Sengjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian, whose courtesy name was Sengjing.

sentences.zh: 元叉之廢靈太后，虔時為千牛備身，與備身張車渠等謀殺叉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Qian was at the time a thousand-ox guard attendant; together with guard attendant Zhang Chequ and others he plotted to kill Cha.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha deposed Empress Dowager Ling, Qian was a thousand-ox guard attendant; together with guard attendant Zhang Chequ and others he plotted to kill Cha.

sentences.zh: 事發，叉殺車渠等，虔坐遠徙。

translations.literal: When the affair broke out Cha killed Chequ and the others, and Qian was punished by distant exile.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered Cha killed Chequ and the others, and Qian was exiled to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，徵為吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule he was summoned as director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling restored her rule he was summoned as director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 太后好以家人禮與親族宴戲，虔常致諫，由是後宴謔多不預焉。

translations.literal: The empress dowager loved to feast and jest with kin by family ceremony; Qian often offered remonstrance, and because of this afterward he was often not present at such banquets and sport.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager loved to feast and jest with kin by family ceremony; Qian often remonstrated, and thereafter he was often absent from such banquets.

sentences.zh: 出為涇州刺史，封安陽縣侯。

translations.literal: He went out as inspector of Jing province and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang county.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as inspector of Jing province and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anyang county.

sentences.zh: 興和三年，以帝元舅超遷司空公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe, as the emperor's maternal uncle by the original line he was promoted over rank to Duke of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Xinghe year 3, as the emperor's maternal uncle he was promoted over rank to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太傅、太尉公、尚書僕射、徐州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Xu province, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand Tutor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Xu province, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 葬日，百官會葬，乘輿送於郭外。

translations.literal: On the day of burial the hundred officials attended the funeral, and the imperial carriage escorted him beyond the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of burial the hundred officials attended the funeral, and the imperial carriage escorted him beyond the city wall.

sentences.zh: 子長粲。

translations.literal: His son was Changcan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Changcan.

sentences.zh: 李延寔，字禧，隴西人，尚書僕射沖之長子。

translations.literal: Li Yanshi, courtesy name Xi, was a man of Longxi and the eldest son of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanshi, whose courtesy name was Xi, was from Longxi and the eldest son of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 性溫良，少為太子舍人。

translations.literal: His nature was gentle and good; in youth he was an attendant of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle by nature, in youth he served as an attendant of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 世宗初，襲父爵清泉縣侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shizong's reign he inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan county.

sentences.zh: [8]累遷左將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: [8] He was repeatedly promoted to Left General and inspector of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: [8] He rose in turn to Left General and inspector of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，以元舅之尊，超授侍中、太保，封濮陽郡王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, by the honor of being the emperor's maternal uncle by the original line he was promoted over rank to Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, as the emperor's maternal uncle he was promoted over rank to Palace Attendant and Grand Guardian and enfeoffed as Prince of Puyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 延寔以太保犯祖諱，又以王爵非庶姓所宜，抗表固辭。

translations.literal: Yanshi, because Grand Guardian violated his ancestor's taboo and because a princely title was not fitting for a common surname, submitted a memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi submitted a firm memorial of refusal, citing the taboo on Grand Guardian and the unsuitability of a princely title for a common surname.

sentences.zh: 徙封濮陽郡公，改授太傅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Duke of Puyang commandery and changed to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Duke of Puyang commandery and made Grand Tutor instead.

sentences.zh: 尋轉司徒公，出為使持節、侍中、太傅、錄尚書事、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Duke of Works and went out as bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Works and went out as bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Tutor, Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Qing province.

sentences.zh: 尒朱兆入洛，乘輿幽縶，以延寔外戚，見害於州館。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang the imperial carriage was held in secret confinement; because Yanshi was a maternal relative by marriage he was killed in the provincial residence.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang the emperor was held in secret confinement; as a maternal kinsman Yanshi was killed in the provincial residence.

sentences.zh: 出帝初，歸葬洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Chu's reign he was returned and buried at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Chu's reign his remains were returned and buried at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、侍中、太師、太尉公、錄尚書事、都督、雍州刺史，諡曰孝懿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing, commander, and inspector of Yong province, with the posthumous name Xiao Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Duke of Grand Marshal, Director of the Masters of Writing, commander, and inspector of Yong province, with the posthumous name Xiao Yi.

sentences.zh: 長子彧，字子文，尚莊帝姊豐亭公主。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yu, courtesy name Ziwen, married Emperor Zhuang's elder sister the Princess of Fengting.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yu, courtesy name Ziwen, married Emperor Zhuang's elder sister the Princess of Fengting.

sentences.zh: 封東平郡公，位侍中、左光祿大夫、中書監、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Swift Cavalry Grand General, opener of an office equal in three matters, and inspector of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Dongping commandery and held the posts of Palace Attendant, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Swift Cavalry Grand General, opener of an office equal in three matters, and inspector of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 彧任俠交遊，輕薄無行。

translations.literal: Yu was chivalrous in fellowship and association, frivolous and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a chivalrous man about town, frivolous and without proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 尒朱榮之死也，武毅之士皆彧所進。

translations.literal: At Erzhu Rong's death the martial and resolute men had all been introduced by Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At Erzhu Rong's death the martial men who took action had all been introduced by Yu.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，以罪棄市。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing he was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojing era he was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：三五哲王，深防遠慮。

translations.literal: The historiographer remarks: The sage kings of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors guarded deeply and planned far.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: The sage kings of the Three Dynasties and Five Emperors took deep precautions and looked far ahead.

sentences.zh: 舅甥之國，罕執鈞衡；

translations.literal: In states of uncles and nephews by marriage, few held the balance of power;
translations.idiomatic: In states ruled through uncles and nephews by marriage, few held the balance of power;

sentences.zh: 母后之家，無聞傾敗。

translations.literal: among the families of empresses dowager and mothers of emperors, none were heard to topple and fail.
translations.idiomatic: among the families of empresses dowager and emperors' mothers, none were heard to topple and fail.

sentences.zh: 爰及後世，顛覆繼軌。

translations.literal: Reaching later ages, overthrow followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: But in later ages overthrow followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 蓋由進不以禮，故其斃亦速。

translations.literal: This was because advancement did not follow ritual, and therefore their destruction was also swift.
translations.idiomatic: This was because advancement did not follow ritual, and therefore their destruction came swiftly as well.

sentences.zh: 其間或不泯舊基，[9]弗虧先構者，蓋處之以道，遠權之所致也。

translations.literal: Among them, those who did not extinguish the old foundation [9] or impair the prior structure were generally those treated by the Way and kept distant from power.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, those who did not extinguish the old foundation [9] or impair what their forebears had built were generally those treated by the Way and kept distant from power.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十三下 諸本目錄此卷注「闕」字，卷末有宋人校語

translations.literal: Book of Wei juan 83b: in the tables of contents of various editions this juan is marked with the character "missing"; at the end of the juan there are collation notes by a Song person
translations.idiomatic: Book of Wei juan 83b: in the tables of contents of various editions this juan is marked "missing"; at the end of the juan there are collation notes by a Song scholar

sentences.zh: 〈殿本入考證〉

translations.literal: 〈Palace edition entered under textual investigation〉
translations.idiomatic: (Palace edition entered under textual investigation)

sentences.zh: 云：「魏收書外戚傳亡，史臣論全用隋書外戚傳

translations.literal: saying: "Wei Shou's treatise on families of imperial consorts is lost; the historiographer's discussion wholly uses the treatise on families of imperial consorts in the Book of Sui
translations.idiomatic: saying: "Wei Shou's treatise on families of imperial consorts is lost; the historiographer's discussion wholly uses the treatise on families of imperial consorts in the Book of Sui

sentences.zh: 〈卷七九〉

translations.literal: 〈juan 79〉
translations.idiomatic: (juan 79)

sentences.zh: 」按此卷亦以北史卷八０外戚傳補。

translations.literal: " According to this, this juan was also supplemented from the treatise on families of imperial consorts in Beishi juan 80.
translations.idiomatic: " According to this, this juan was also supplemented from the treatise on families of imperial consorts in Beishi juan 80.

sentences.zh: 其于勁傳採北史卷三一于栗磾附于勁傳，李延寔傳採卷一００自序。

translations.literal: Its treatise on Yu Jin draws on the appended treatise on Yu Jin in Beishi juan 31 under Yu Libi; the treatise on Li Yanshi draws on the autobiographical preface in juan 100.
translations.idiomatic: Its treatise on Yu Jin draws on the appended treatise on Yu Jin in Beishi juan 31 under Yu Libi; the treatise on Li Yanshi draws on the autobiographical preface in juan 100.

sentences.zh: 諸傳均有溢出語，當是以高氏小史等他書附益之。

translations.literal: All the treatises have overflow language, which should have been added from other books such as the Brief History of the Gao clan.
translations.idiomatic: All the treatises contain extraneous passages, likely added from other books such as the Brief History of the Gao clan.

sentences.zh: 自栗磾至勁

translations.literal: From Li Bi to Jin
translations.idiomatic: From Li Bi to Jin

translations.literal: 〈to〉
