sentences.zh: 三開國公 按此數語魏書本在卷三一于栗磾附于忠傳後，北史卷二三于栗磾傳移在于勁傳中，則在後的于忠所歷官爵，不當計算在內，所舉贈公、領軍、尚書令、開國公便都少了一人，實誤。

translations.literal: three founding-state dukes: According to this, these words in the Book of Wei originally stood after the appended treatise on Yu Zhong in juan 31 under Yu Libi; the Beishi treatise on Yu Libi in juan 23 moved them into the treatise on Yu Jin, so the offices and titles held by the later Yu Zhong should not be counted within; the cited posthumous dukes, palace commanders, directors of the Masters of Writing, and founding-state dukes are each one person short—an actual error.
translations.idiomatic: three founding-state dukes: These words in the Book of Wei originally stood after the appended treatise on Yu Zhong in juan 31 under Yu Libi; the Beishi treatise on Yu Libi in juan 23 moved them into the treatise on Yu Jin, so the later offices of Yu Zhong should not be counted; each category of posthumous duke, palace commander, director of the Masters of Writing, and founding-state duke is one short—an actual error.

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，不記卷三一已有此語，以致複出。

translations.literal: This treatise was supplemented from the Beishi and did not record that juan 31 already had this language, causing duplication.
translations.idiomatic: This treatise was supplemented from the Beishi without noting that juan 31 already contained this passage, causing duplication.

sentences.zh: 參卷三一校記[九]。

translations.literal: See collation note [9] in juan 31.
translations.idiomatic: See collation note [9] in juan 31.

sentences.zh: 高平郡都將 按郡無都將，「郡」當是「鎮」之訛。

translations.literal: Commander of Gaoping commandery: According to this, a commandery has no commander-in-chief; "commandery" should be a corruption of "garrison."
translations.idiomatic: Commander of Gaoping commandery: A commandery has no commander-in-chief; "commandery" should be a corruption of "garrison."

sentences.zh: 熙平初 諸本及北史卷八０胡國珍傳「熙平」作「延和」，通志卷一六五胡國珍傳作「熙平中」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiping: in various editions and in the treatise on Hu Guozhen in Beishi juan 80 "Xiping" is written as "Yanhe"; in the treatise on Hu Guozhen in Tongzhi juan 165 it is written as "in Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiping: in various editions and in the treatise on Hu Guozhen in Beishi juan 80 "Xiping" reads "Yanhe"; in the treatise on Hu Guozhen in Tongzhi juan 165 it reads "in Xiping."

sentences.zh: 按事見卷九肅宗紀熙平元年八月乙巳，延和乃拓跋燾年號，遠在其前。

translations.literal: According to this, the event appears in the annals of Emperor Suzong in juan 9, eighth month, day yisi of the first year of Xiping; Yanhe is the era name of Tuoba Tao, far earlier.
translations.idiomatic: The event appears in the annals of Emperor Suzong in juan 9, eighth month, day yisi of Xiping year 1; Yanhe is the era name of Tuoba Tao, far earlier.

sentences.zh: 今據通志改作「熙平」。

translations.literal: Now following the Tongzhi it is changed to "Xiping."
translations.idiomatic: Following the Tongzhi it is here changed to "Xiping."

sentences.zh: 事在元年，「初」字不誤。

translations.literal: The event is in the first year; the character "beginning" is not in error.
translations.idiomatic: The event falls in the first year; the word "beginning" is not in error.

sentences.zh: 又追京兆郡君為秦太上君 按「追」下當脫「贈」或「尊」「崇」字。

translations.literal: Further posthumously honoring Lady of Jingzhao commandery as Grand Lord of Qin: According to this, below "posthumously" there should be a missing character "grant," "honor," or "exalt."
translations.idiomatic: Further posthumously honoring Lady of Jingzhao commandery as Grand Lord of Qin: Below "posthumously" a word such as "grant," "honor," or "exalt" is likely missing.

sentences.zh: 持節就安定監護喪事 按胡國珍死和葬都在洛陽，何故「就安定監護喪事」？

translations.literal: Bearer of the staff of authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral rites: According to this, Hu Guozhen's death and burial were both at Luoyang—why "went to Anding to supervise the funeral rites"?
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the staff of authority went to Anding to supervise the funeral rites: Hu Guozhen died and was buried at Luoyang—why "went to Anding to supervise the funeral rites"?

sentences.zh: 下文云：「迎太上君神柩還第」，疑「安定」下脫「公第」二字。

translations.literal: The text below says: "welcomed the Grand Lord's spirit coffin back to the residence"—it is suspected that below "Anding" the two characters "duke's residence" are missing.
translations.idiomatic: The text below says "welcomed the Grand Lord's spirit coffin back to the residence"—"Anding" likely omits the two characters "duke's residence."

sentences.zh: 真長子寧 諸本「真」字連上段「諡曰孝」，「長子寧」提行。

translations.literal: Zhen's eldest son Ning: in various editions the character "Zhen" is joined to the preceding passage "posthumous name Xiao," and "eldest son Ning" begins a new line.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's eldest son Ning: in various editions the character "Zhen" is joined to the preceding passage "posthumous name Xiao," and "eldest son Ning" begins a new line.

sentences.zh: 成為胡僧洗諡「孝真」，「寧」是僧洗的長子。

translations.literal: Forming Hu Sengxi's posthumous name "Xiao Zhen"; "Ning" is Sengxi's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Forming Hu Sengxi's posthumous name "Xiao Zhen"; "Ning" is Sengxi's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 按真乃國珍兄，見上文，寧乃僧洗兄。

translations.literal: According to this, Zhen was Guozhen's elder brother, seen in the text above; Ning was Sengxi's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was Guozhen's elder brother, as seen above; Ning was Sengxi's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 北史原文本不提行，後人寫刻魏書則凡附見諸子孫無不提行，這裏由於誤讀，提行亦謬，致以兄為子，今改正。

translations.literal: The original text of the Beishi did not begin a new line; later persons writing and carving the Book of Wei invariably began new lines for all appended sons and grandsons; here through misreading the new line is also wrong, causing an elder brother to be taken as a son—now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The Beishi original did not begin a new line; later editors of the Book of Wei invariably began new lines for all appended descendants; here misreading caused a wrong line break, making an elder brother appear as a son—now corrected.

sentences.zh: 襲父爵清泉縣侯 按卷五三李沖傳，沖封「清淵縣侯」。

translations.literal: Inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan county: According to the treatise on Li Chong in juan 53, Chong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingyuan county.
translations.idiomatic: Inherited his father's title as Marquis of Qingquan county: According to the treatise on Li Chong in juan 53, Chong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qingyuan county.

sentences.zh: 「清淵」為漢以來舊縣，卷一０六上地形志上，屬司州陽平郡。

translations.literal: "Qingyuan" is an old county since Han; in the Treatise on Geography A in juan 106 it belongs to Yangping commandery in Si province.
translations.idiomatic: "Qingyuan" is an old county since Han; in the Treatise on Geography A in juan 106 it belongs to Yangping commandery in Si province.

sentences.zh: 此傳以北史補，避唐諱改「泉」。

translations.literal: This treatise was supplemented from the Beishi; to avoid Tang taboo it was changed to "quan."
translations.idiomatic: This treatise was supplemented from the Beishi; to avoid Tang taboo "yuan" was changed to "quan."

sentences.zh: 其間或不泯舊基 諸本「泯」上有「斃」字。

translations.literal: Among them those who did not extinguish the old foundation: in various editions above "extinguish" there is the character "destroy."
translations.idiomatic: Among them those who did not extinguish the old foundation: in various editions the character "destroy" appears above "extinguish."

sentences.zh: 此傳本出北史，北史傳論又本隋書卷七九外戚傳論，今檢隋書、北史都作「今或不隕舊基」，這裏「今或」作「其間」，「隕」作「泯」，均兩通，「斃」字則涉上「其斃亦速」而衍，今刪。

translations.literal: This treatise originally comes from the Beishi; the Beishi treatise discussion in turn comes from the discussion in the treatise on families of imperial consorts in the Book of Sui juan 79; now checking the Book of Sui and Beishi both read "now perhaps not falling from the old foundation"; here "now perhaps" is written as "among them" and "fall" as "extinguish"—both are acceptable; the character "destroy" was interpolated from the preceding "their destruction was also swift"—now deleted.
translations.idiomatic: This treatise comes from the Beishi; its discussion in turn comes from the Book of Sui juan 79; both the Book of Sui and Beishi read "now perhaps not falling from the old foundation"; here "now perhaps" reads "among them" and "fall" reads "extinguish"—both are acceptable; "destroy" was interpolated from the preceding "their destruction came swiftly" and is now deleted.
